findings.quote: E)  A horizontal block in row \(r=5\), columns \(c=2,3,4\).
findings.reason: Blocks C and E overlap at (5,2), so these five blocks cannot all be torn out as disjoint intact blocks.

findings.quote: Thus after tearing out these \(5\) blocks in each \(5\times5\) cell there is no triple left anywhere in the \(n\times n\) square.
findings.reason: Even deleting the union of the listed cells leaves the horizontal triple (1,1),(1,2),(1,3) untouched in every macrosquare. Thus the asserted blocking property is false.

judgment.reason: The lower-bound counting argument works for n≥2, with n=1 trivial. The upper-bound construction has overlapping blocks and leaves available triples, so it does not prove the theorem.
unresolved_obligations: Establish the upper bound using a legal maximal collection of at most n²/5 + O(n) disjoint blocks.
